title: Generative AI in Senior Design: 7 Rules
description: Seven practical rules for using generative AI in an engineering capstone while preserving verification, safety, standards, evidence, and student ownership.

pages.heading: Using Generative AI in Senior Design? Follow These 7 Rules
pages.text: AI can speed up exploration, code and documentation. Your team still owns every engineering decision and result.
pages.alt: Engineering capstone team using an AI assistant while building and testing a robotic prototype

pages.heading: 1. Explore, Don't Outsource
pages.text: Ask AI for design alternatives, then compare them against requirements, constraints, risks and trade-offs before choosing.
pages.alt: Mechanical engineering student comparing several AI-assisted thermal-system design alternatives

pages.heading: 2. Verify Equations and Units
pages.text: Re-derive critical steps, check dimensions, inspect assumptions and test boundary cases. A confident AI answer can still be wrong.
pages.alt: Electrical engineering student verifying equations and units with a calculator and laboratory instruments

pages.heading: 3. Test Every Line of Code
pages.text: Run unit tests, compare with a baseline, inspect edge cases and reproduce the output. Working once is not validation.
pages.alt: Engineering student testing AI-assisted control code against a robot and simulation

pages.heading: 4. Check Specs and Standards
pages.text: Verify components, ratings, tolerances and safety rules in official datasheets and applicable standards—not an AI summary.
pages.alt: Engineering team checking component specifications and safety standards against measured prototype data

pages.heading: 5. Keep an AI Decision Log
pages.text: Record prompts, useful outputs, rejected suggestions, human edits, tests and final decisions so your process remains explainable.
pages.alt: Capstone student documenting the traceable sequence from AI prompts to reviewed engineering decisions

pages.heading: 6. Protect Project Data
pages.text: Follow your university's policy. Do not upload confidential research, sponsor data, personal information or restricted designs without permission.
pages.alt: Engineering student protecting confidential project files before using an AI tool

pages.heading: 7. Defend the Trade-offs
pages.text: Be ready to explain why the design works, how you tested it, where it can fail and why you rejected the alternatives.
pages.alt: Student defending an AI-assisted engineering capstone with a tested prototype and evidence

pages.heading: AI Assists. Engineers Decide.
pages.text: ABET's 2026–27 criteria still center design, standards, constraints, experimentation, communication, ethics and engineering judgment.
pages.alt: Capstone team taking ownership of an AI-assisted engineering design and its verified results
